.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
No changes were made to the forecast. 

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
- 1) Below average temperatures and mainly dry conditions are
  expected into the weekend.

- 2) Returning to a summer-like pattern next week.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
KEY MESSAGE 1...Below average temperatures and mainly dry
conditions are expected into the weekend. 

Surface high pressure, originating from Canada, remains overhead
today before slowly shifting towards New England. Below normal
temperatures are expected today and tomorrow with highs in the
70s to low 80s. Southerly winds bring increased cloud cover
today with an upper level trough yielding a slight chance of
rain showers in the southern portions of the forecast area.
Precipitation chances continue Saturday afternoon, mainly along
the I-81 corridor in the afternoon before conditions dry out
overnight. Sunday will be the warmest day of the weekend with 
highs in the 70s to upper 80s with dry conditions expected. 

KEY MESSAGE 2...Returning to a summer-like pattern next week.

Coming off of the weekend, an upper-level trough begins to dig into 
the northeastern U.S. This will usher in the potential for organized 
convection early to mid week. In spite of multiple frontal passages 
during the period, next week could carry a return to summer-like 
conditions with heat indices in the mid 90s to near 100 degrees.

The key players will be a longstanding upper ridge across the 
southwestern U.S. into the southern/central Great Plains, a deep 
upper low near Hudson Bay, and longwave trough over the eastern U.S. 
While ensemble solutions do not show a more formidable shortwave 
tracking across the area, the setup certainly lends itself to a more 
active pattern. A series of "ridge rollers" are likely to cross the 
northern tier of the country before crossing the Great Lakes and 
northeastern states. At this juncture, the machine-learning 
algorithms favor an uptick in convection on Monday into Tuesday. 
This would present the most likely opportunity for any severe 
thunderstorms. A progressive pattern aloft will bring a cold front 
through the region on Tuesday evening/night, with a secondary 
boundary on its heels. While temperatures remain seasonable in this 
mid/late week pattern shift, dew points slowly come down to finish 
out the month of July.

&&

.AVIATION /06Z FRIDAY THROUGH TUESDAY/...
VFR conditions and light winds are expected today and through
the weekend as high pressure remains over the mid atlantic. 
Southeast winds today and Saturday become north/northeasterly 
Sunday. 

With the shift toward a more active pattern, expect an increase in 
convective-driven restrictions on Monday into Tuesday. Between 
the pair of days, the arrival of a cold front on Tuesday would 
aid in a better shot for severe storms. Outside of convection, 
expect VFR conditions to largely remain. Overall winds generally
waver between southwest to westerly, with afternoon gusts to 
around 15 to 20 knots.

&&

.MARINE...
No hazardous conditions are expected over the waters today 
through the weekend. Light winds and dry conditions continue
through Sunday with winds expected to stay below Small Craft
Advisory criteria. 

There is an increasing signal of southerly channeling for Monday 
evening into the night. If this continues, Small Craft Advisories 
may be needed for portions of the Chesapeake Bay. This could linger 
a bit longer into Tuesday morning over southern portions of the bay 
waters. Otherwise, the bigger story is the increasing convective 
threats for early next week. Special Marine Warnings may be needed 
for any of the stronger thunderstorms, particularly on Tuesday as a 
cold front moves through.

&&

.TIDES/COASTAL FLOODING...
Tidal anomalies rebound within onshore flow this weekend, with 
more sensitive locations potentially reaching Action Stage this
morning and through the weekend. Annapolis could approach minor
flood thresholds by Sat night.
